chapter: Union, publishers, race and Harlem nightlife
title: No musicians' club; kickbacks ended
summary: He recalls no musicians' society and says kickbacks ended about 20 years ago.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: Jay C., what I'm trying to get at is like, in my home town in Detroit we had a musician's club as kids. We used to have a little society where we used to gather and discuss about music and problems. If some club owner wasn't doing right we'd black-ball him as musicians, say don't do this, don't work over here, don't have nothing to do with this person. Did you have anything like that?
He's talking about Detroit. In New York?

A social club, a social type thing... Like at the Metropole you said the guy would pay the band $100 to the union, pay them $100 and send the money over. You'd get your $100 and then go back and have to give this guy, the owner of the club, $30 kickback.
That's wrong, I knew that a long time ago.
What I'm saying is, now, things like that the musicians spoke about. Did they ever say, well listen, you know, like you
better watch out for this guy because you work in his club and you have to give him a kickback?

No. That left about 20 years ago because, see, you have your scales. If they hire me and the Metropole was open and I go in there, this comes from 802. I have to report to them first and they tell me the scales, how much tax I have to pay each week, and that's what I have to pay. If I don't make but a dollar and a half a week and they pay me a thousand dollars a week, they can't take out but a dollar and a half a week, and the rest of the money goes to me.
